ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the graph of the inverse proportion function $y=\frac{k}{x}$ $(x>0)$ passes through points A and B. Draw $AC\perp y$ axis at point C through A, and draw $BD\perp y$ axis at point D through B. Also, draw $BE\perp x$ axis at point E through B, and connect AD. It is known that $AC=1$, $BE=1$, and the area of rectangle $BDOE$ is $4$. Then, what is the area of $\triangle ACD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Construct AH $\perp$ x-axis at point H, intersecting BD at point F, \\
$\therefore$ Quadrilateral ACOH, quadrilateral ACDF, quadrilateral ODBE are all rectangles, \\
$\because$ The area of rectangle BDOE is 4, and the inverse proportion function $y=\frac{k}{x}$ (x＞0) passes through point B, with k＞0, \\
$\therefore$k＝4 \\
$\therefore$The area of rectangle ACOH is 4, \\
$\because$AC＝1 \\
$\therefore$OC＝4÷1＝4, \\
$\therefore$CD＝OC−OD＝OC−BE＝4−1＝3, \\
$\therefore$The area of rectangle ACDF＝1×3＝3, \\
$\therefore$${S}_{\triangle ACD}=\frac{1}{2}{S}_{\text{rectangle }CDFA}=\boxed{\frac{3}{2}}$.

ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: As shown in the figure, the graph of the inverse proportion function $y=\frac{k}{x}$ $(x>0)$ passes through points A and B. Draw $AC\perp y$ axis at point C through A, and draw $BD\perp y$ axis at point D through B. Also, draw $BE\perp x$ axis at point E through B, and connect AD. It is known that $AC=1$, $BE=1$, and the area of rectangle $BDOE$ is $4$. Then, what is the area of $\triangle ACD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.expected_answer: \textbf{Solution:} Construct $AH\perp x$-axis at point H, intersecting $BD$ at point F. Therefore quadrilateral $ACOH$, quadrilateral $ACDF$, and quadrilateral $ODBE$ are all rectangles. Because the area of rectangle $BDOE$ is $4$, and the inverse proportion function $y=\frac{k}{x}$ $(x>0)$ passes through point $B$, we have $k=4$. Therefore the area of rectangle $ACOH$ is $4$. Because $AC=1$, therefore $OC=4\div 1=4$. Therefore $CD=OC-OD=OC-BE=4-1=3$. Therefore the area of rectangle $ACDF=1\times 3=3$. Hence ${S}_{\triangle ACD}=\frac{1}{2}{S}_{\text{rectangle }CDFA}=\boxed{\frac{3}{2}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure there are coordinate axes, O is the origin, the x-axis points to the right, and the y-axis points upward; the inverse proportional function curve is located in the first quadrant and passes through points A and B. From point A, draw a horizontal line to the left to the y-axis, intersecting at C, so AC is the horizontal distance from A to the y-axis; from point B, draw a horizontal line to the left to the y-axis, intersecting at D, and draw a vertical line downward to the x-axis, intersecting at E. In the figure, rectangle BDOE is located near the coordinate axes, and C is above D. Reasoning: According to the coordinate relationships in the figure, let A=(1,a), because AC=1 means the x-coordinate of A is 1. Let B=(b,1), because BE=1 means the y-coordinate of B is 1. The side lengths of rectangle BDOE are b and 1, and its area is 4, so b·1=4, obtaining b=4, that is, B=(4,1). B is on y=k/x, therefore k=4·1=4. A is also on the same inverse proportional function, and the x-coordinate of A is 1, so a=4/1=4, A=(1,4). Thus C=(0,4), D=(0,1), so CD=4-1=3. Triangle ACD takes AC=1 and CD=3 as two mutually perpendicular sides, and its area is (1/2)·1·3=3/2.
